title: Chain annotation sprint — heuristics & quick lit digest
content:
Goal: fast heuristics + minimal schema for annotating multi-step reasoning traces (human-in-the-loop)

Context / why now:
- Need robust labels for short/long chain-of-thought (CoT) units to train/eval safety filters and automated critique models.
- Downstream: quality regressions when quantizing models and when switching to hyphenated attention kernels — we need targeted probes.

Quick lit skim (notes + what matters for labeling):
1) "Efficient Transformer Variants" (notes: generic survey) — takeaways: truncation artifacts often show up as abrupt final-step hallucinations; labelers should mark "abrupt_finish" when conclusion incoheres with previous step.
2) "Synthetic Chains and Calibration" (workshop paper) — synthetic chains help bootstrap calibrator but miss contextual grounding; add flag "grounding_needed" when the chain references external facts but no citation provided.
3) "Human CoT Eval Metrics" (short paper) — proposes step-level correctness & novelty. Important: allow "partial_credit" for steps that are directionally right but missing numeric rigor.

Proposed lightweight schema (for sprint): each chain = header metadata + list of steps. Fields we actually ask annotators to fill (min effort):
- chain_id (auto)
- prompt_type: RETRIEVAL | PROBLEM_SOLVE | OPEN_ENDED
- claim_at_end: short free text (1 line)
- global_veracity: TRUE | FALSE | UNDECIDED
- step_n text (annotator copies step)
- step_label: CORRECT | INCORRECT | PLAUSIBLE_BUT_MISSING | HALLUCINATE | AMBIGUOUS
- step_reason: (1–2 short bullets)
- step_evidence: NONE | CITED | RECALLABLE
- abort_flag: ABRUPT_FINISH | LOOPING | CONTRADICTORY
- confidence (1–3)

Heuristic rules for labelers (cheat sheet):
- If step contains a factual numeric claim (date, count, code), prefer CORRECT/INCORRECT after quick web check (30s). If can’t verify in 30s, mark PLAUSIBLE_BUT_MISSING.
- For multi-step derivations: mark step as CORRECT only if intermediate operation is valid (e.g., algebraic step preserves equality).
- When chain cites retrieval doc but quote is misaligned -> HALLUCINATE + cite source mismatch in step_reason.
- If chain repeats same assertion without adding new support, mark LOOPING on abort_flag.

Annotation UX friction points (observed in pilot):
- Copying long tokens into web search breaks formatting — add "search-sanitizer" utility to strip newlines and code fences.
- Annotator burnout: steps > 15 should be chunked across two sessions with a 10m cooldown.
- Borderline cases: when a chain blends reasoning + fictional premise (roleplay), use prompt_type = OPEN_ENDED and set global_veracity = UNDECIDED.

Small experiment plan (week-long sprint):
- Day 0: seed 200 chains (mix of retrieval/problem_solve/open_ended) from hosted-api logs (samples anonymized).
- Day 1–2: 3 annotators label 50 chains each using schema; capture time-per-step and friction notes.
- Day 3: adjudication on 30 contested chains to create gold standard.
- Day 4: quick model to predict step_label from step text (toy classifier) — baseline with bag-of-n-grams + evidence_flag.
- Day 5: retrospective + refine schema.

Metrics to capture:
- throughput: steps/hour per annotator
- disagreement rate (step_label)
- percent_of_steps_with_evidence
- average_time_for_verification (web-check)

Sample annotated examples (handy templates for tooltips):
- Example A (retrieval): chain ends with a claim about an event date. Annotator check -> found contradictory source -> step_label=INCORRECT, step_reason="source X says 2019 not 2021"; abort_flag=NONE
- Example B (math derivation): three steps, middle step drops a term -> mark middle INCORRECT + partial_credit on final if rest still reaches right numeric result.
- Example C (roleplay fiction): clearly fictional premise -> prompt_type=OPEN_ENDED, global_veracity=UNDECIDED, all steps PLAUSIBLE_BUT_MISSING

Tooling notes (what I will ask product/eng for):
- small annotation UI: copy/paste step, quick radio buttons for labels, evidence URL field, one-click "search" that opens sanitized query.
- export format: CSV with chain_id, step_index, step_text, step_label, step_reason (short), evidence_url, annotator_id, time_ms.
- slack command /chain-anno to push interesting examples to #model-failures

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: threshold for "partial_credit" — define precisely: is it "maintains logical flow" OR "reaches correct final answer despite one incorrect intermediate"? (action: adjudicate examples)
- Q2: how to handle sensitive content in chains? flag for S&C review or redact before sending to crowd workers? (action: propose redaction pipeline)
- Q3: sampling bias — hosted-api logs skew to short chains; need a deliberate sample of long (>20 step) chains. (action: query logs)

References and quick links I keep re-reading:
- arXiv: synthetic chain calibration (see linked_artifacts)
- repo: redwood-inference/chain-annotation-templates (for CSV schema)
- Slack: #evals pinned thread (example adjudication notes)

Notes to self before sprint kickoff:
- Print cheat sheet and make it single page.
- Run a 30 min alignment sync with annotators — go through 5 golden examples.
- Build a small web-sanitizer script and upload to shared drive under /users/tools.

Random half-baked ideas:
- Use contrastive pairs: present annotator with two chains that reach same final claim but one used retrieval -> see if they prefer one as higher quality. Good signal for retrieval-worthiness.
- Lightweight "explainability" ask: for each INCORRECT step, have annotator propose a 1-line correction. Could be used to auto-generate training data for critic models.

Status: ready to seed initial 200 chains once I get sample export (Riya to run query).
